title: arXiv Physics Daily — Friday, 30 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from limited community-attention and curation signals plus paper-specific results, with little usable citation evidence for such recent submissions. It is not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days
sections.abstract: The authors give end-to-end physical-resource estimates for compiling Shor's algorithm onto two superconducting cat-qubit architectures, including layouts and schedules for RSA-2048 and related discrete-log benchmarks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: SciRate's Top arXiv papers feed surfaced it among its leading entries at the snapshot, a qualitative community-attention signal; no numerical score is used.
sections.claimed_result: The authors estimate RSA-2048 factoring at 22,593 cat qubits and 3.14 days under their stated hardware and noise assumptions; the RSA circuit is compiled in full, while related estimates reuse its operations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; circuit compilation, error-correction resource modeling, physical-qubit layouts, and schedules
sections.unique_caveat: The headline estimate assumes a 1 μs error-correction cycle, 10 μs decoder reaction, phase-flip probability 5×10⁻⁴, and no bit flips—roughly a 100-year bit-flip time. The authors give a higher-cost alternative when bit flips are included; this is a resource estimate, not a demonstration of a working machine.

sections.title: High-Fidelity Universal Quantum Gates in a Cryogenic Atom Array
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate a universal gate set in a cryogenic ¹³³Cs tweezer array, reporting 99.970(2)% single-qubit fidelity and 99.76(8)% raw two-qubit entangling-gate fidelity using direct single-photon Rydberg excitation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A community-maintained quantum-experiment index opened a paper-addition issue on 30 October; the paper is also cross-listed between atomic physics and quantum physics, and reports measured gate benchmarks.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a complete universal gate set in a cryogenic atom array; their error analysis attributes most measured two-qubit infidelity to atomic motion, with the Rydberg-decay contribution below 3×10⁻⁴.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; cryogenic optical-tweezer array of ¹³³Cs atoms, with single- and two-qubit gate benchmarking
sections.unique_caveat: Atomic motion remains the dominant error in the measured gate, so the higher fidelities projected from suppressing Rydberg decay require improved cooling and further experimental validation.

sections.title: A $B_{1g}$ phonon unlocks $d$-wave superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model
sections.abstract: Finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo calculations find a $d$-wave superconducting dome when a $B_{1g}$ phonon couples to the doped repulsive $t$-$t'$ Hubbard model, with the authors reporting cooperative enhancement beyond either interaction alone.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Its cross-listing links superconductivity and strongly correlated electrons, and the paper reports finite-temperature numerical evidence for a concrete pairing mechanism. No paper-specific citation or independent discussion signal was found in the sources checked, so its placement reflects the result rather than measured attention.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a transition scale near $T_c/t≈0.04$ at $U/t=1$ and density 0.8, with a doping dome; this establishes a result in the simulated model, not in a material sample.
sections.evidence_type: computational; numerically exact determinant quantum Monte Carlo on doped Hubbard-model lattices
sections.unique_caveat: The fermion sign problem limits access to lower temperatures at stronger repulsion and prevents equally direct checks on the largest lattices; finite-size and extrapolation limits therefore remain relevant.

sections.title: Disentangling constraints on $S_8$ from the high and low redshift CMB
sections.abstract: A principal-component analysis separates primordial-CMB and CMB-lensing contributions to clustering constraints, finding a primordial-CMB $S_8$ value compatible with DES while the lensing-inferred clustering is higher.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work appears in multiple third-party daily arXiv listings, including DailyArXiV and Academus, and combines Planck, ACT, and SPT data with an explicit comparison to DES.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain $S_8=0.795±0.022$ from the primordial CMB, consistent with their cited DES value of $0.789±0.012$; the size of the lensing excess and the comparison depend on the prior for summed neutrino mass.
sections.evidence_type: observational; reanalysis of Planck 2018, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G D1 CMB data, compared with Dark Energy Survey results
sections.unique_caveat: This is a data-analysis separation, not evidence that a cosmological tension is resolved; the authors report sensitivity to the neutrino-mass prior and lensing treatment.

sections.title: Neutrino electromagnetic properties after the first $pp$ solar neutrino observation at XENONnT
sections.abstract: The authors analyze XENONnT's reported low-energy solar-neutrino scattering data to infer the $pp$ flux and low-momentum-transfer weak mixing angle, and to constrain several neutrino electromagnetic interactions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A curated 30 October neutrino/particle-physics arXiv digest selected the work; it links a newly available low-energy detector data set to several beyond-Standard-Model constraints.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive bounds on neutrino charge radii, magnetic moments, millicharges, and a sterile-neutrino dipole portal from the published XENONnT data; they specifically test how the mild $pp$-flux excess is affected by the $^{14}$C background.
sections.evidence_type: observational; phenomenological fit to the XENONnT collaboration's reported neutrino-electron scattering result, not a new detector measurement
sections.unique_caveat: The mild flux excess and the $^{14}$C background treatment affect the fitted quantities, so the inferred constraints depend on the background model and data interpretation.
